main_text.p: excciderit Paulina illa ad Hebræos & interversa fuerit, quod affirmare proclive, probare operosum; vel hanc ipsam, de cujus authore controvertitur, innuerit Petrus ac designarit.
main_text.head: II.
main_text.p: Itaque in eo imprimis vis tota probationis consistit, compellari à Petro Hebræos, iisque posteriorem hanc inscriptâ. Patet id vel ex Capite ejusdem tertio, sub initium. Ταύτην ἤδη, ἀγαπητοὶ, δευτέραν ὑμῖν γράφω ἐπιστολὴν, ἐν αἷς διεγείρω &c. Iisdem ergò data hæc Epistola cum priori. Hinc δευτέρα, hinc pariter Catholica, ut ex titulo & inscriptione, hinc paris etiam argumenti, ut ex collatione liquet. Quare assurgendum ad Παυλείαν Epistolæ prioris, quæ habet ἐκλεκτοῖς, παροικήμασις, διασπορᾶς Ποντ, Γαλατίας, Καππαδοκίας, Ἀσίας & Bιθυνίας. Iudæos sive Hebræos intelligi constat sanè. 1. quod παροίκους illos dicit, seu παροίκους, ξένους, ἀλλοεθνεῖς, ἀλλοφύλας, advenas, peregrinos inter gentes: quod in Iudæos patriis sedibus motos & extrà Iudææ pomœria alibi terrarum vicitantes, per belle quadrat. 11. page.notes: Greek passages are transcribed as read; several Greek words in the scan are partly illegible (notably the second and third lines of the Greek). The word "dia-" at the bottom right is a catchword. Some letters in the Greek may be slightly off due to print damage; treat the Greek as approximate and check against the scan. Printing errors such as "excciderit" (probably "exciderit") and "Hebræos" with Hebræos spelling are left as printed. The "II." heading is a numbered paragraph marker and could arguably be a plain paragraph opener.
